results.title: Rédei's $g$ from the bits
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $V$ be a finite set with bits $a_{ij}\in\mathbb F_2$ ($i,j\in V$) and $y_i,z_i\in\mathbb F_2$ ($i\in V$). For $S\subseteq V$ write $y(S)=\sum_{i\in S}y_i$ and $z(S)=\sum_{i\in S}z_i$. The bits satisfy *reciprocity* if $a_{ij}+a_{ji}=y_iy_j$ for all $i\ne j$ in $V$.

results.title: The genus sum $T_{5b}$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $a,y,z$ be bits on a finite set $V$. A set $B\subseteq V$ has *class* $1$, $5$, $7$ or $3$ according as $(y(B),z(B))$ is $(0,0)$, $(0,1)$, $(1,0)$ or $(1,1)$. The *genus sum of row 5b* of the bits is the sum over the set partitions $\pi$ of $V$ (into nonempty blocks) with exactly one block of class $7$, exactly one block of class $3$ and no block of class $5$, so that all other blocks have class $1$.

results.title: The root factors of a marked partition
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $y,z$ be bits on a finite set $V$, $f$ a forest on $V$ with root set $R$, and write $z^S=\prod_{\rho\in S}z_\rho$. For blocks $B_7,B_3$ and a block $B$, the *root factor* $e_B(S)$ of a set $S$ is $y_\rho+z_\rho$ if $B=B_7$ and $S=\{\rho\}$; $z_\rho$ if $B=B_3\ne B_7$ and $S=\{\rho\}$; $z^S$ if $B\notin\{B_7,B_3\}$ and $|S|=2$; and $0$ in all other cases.

results.title: Compatible partitions with one or two roots per block
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be a forest on a finite set $V$ with root set $R$, and let $E\subseteq R$. The set partitions compatible with $f$ in which every root in $E$ is the only root of its block and every block containing a root outside $E$ contains exactly two roots are as many as the fixed-point-free involutions of $R\setminus E$. For $E=R$ there is exactly one.

results.title: $\det M_1$ as a sum over partitions into class-3 blocks (Proposition 3.3)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $a,y,z$ be bits on a finite set $V$ that satisfy reciprocity. Then the first sum over the set partitions $\pi$ of $V$ into blocks of class $3$, the second over the forests $f$ on $V$, with $R$ the root set of $f$. If $y(V)=0$, then $\det M_1$ is the same sum over the partitions into blocks of class $3$; if $y(V)=1$, then $\det M_1=0$.
